## Motivation
Clinical trials are essential to advancing medical knowledge and developing new treatments, yet the distribution of clinical research across diseases and geographic regions may not reflect different populations' health needs. Understanding whether clinical research priorities align with the conditions responsible for the greatest disease burden could reveal geographic disparities in research activity and potential gaps in global health research.

Using publicly available data from ClinicalTrials.gov, AACT, and WHO Global Health Estimates, our project aims to examine geographic and temporal trends in clinical trial activity and evaluate how closely research distribution across disease categories aligns with country-specific disease burden, measured in disability-adjusted life years (DALYs).

## Anticipated data sources: 
We will use the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database for study identifiers, conditions and MeSH terms, locations, start dates, study type, phase, enrollment, and sponsor information. We will link these records to WHO estimates of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) by cause and country. We will finalize disease categories, geographic coverage, and the trial-start and burden-reference periods after assessing data availability and compatibility.
## Intended Final Products 
We will develop an interactive website presenting our research questions, data preparation, visualizations, key findings, and limitations. Deliverables will also include a written report, a narrated two-minute screencast, and a GitHub repository with reproducible R Markdown analyses.

## Planned Analyses:
Geographic distribution: Interactive world maps showing the number and distribution of registered clinical trials across countries.
Disease-specific research priorities: Classify clinical trials into broader disease categories using MeSH terms and compare the most frequently studied conditions across countries.
Temporal trends: Examine changes in clinical trial activity across disease categories from 2015–2025 (for example)
Trial characteristics: Compare sponsor types across countries and disease categories.
Research priorities vs. disease burden: Compare the proportion of clinical trials investigating different disease categories with the proportion of country-specific disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to those conditions.

## Visualizations
Planned visualizations include paired maps of disease burden and research activity, scatterplots comparing their shares, and heatmaps summarizing differences across countries and diseases. We will also explore whether these patterns differ between industry and other lead-sponsor categories.

## Coding Challenges

The main coding challenges will be mapping AACT condition and MeSH terms to WHO cause categories, harmonizing country identifiers and periods, handling missing data, and preventing duplicate counts when joining tables. We will specify counting rules for multinational and multiple-condition trials and assess how alternative rules affect our comparisons. Interpretation will acknowledge that AACT represents ClinicalTrials.gov registrations and that trial locations do not directly measure local enrollment, research spending, or access to treatment.
